content.subject: Trying to understand how the statute actually applies to my fall
content.body:
Hello,

I am following up on the premises-liability matter I came in about last month, where I fell on the staircase at the shopping plaza. My adjuster mentioned that there is a specific state statute that governs the duty owed by a property owner to someone in my position, and that how the statute gets interpreted by the courts is really the heart of the case.

I would like the firm to put together a short written explanation of how that statute applies to my facts. Please quote the operative language from the statute itself, give me the proper citation so I can look it up, and then walk through how the courts in this state have interpreted each of the key elements, with the leading interpretive decisions cited. If there is any meaningful disagreement among the appellate divisions on what a particular element requires, please flag that and cite the cases going each direction.

I am not asking for a brief, just a plain-English memo with the supporting authority cited inline so I can verify the reasoning. I learn better when I can see the source material myself.

Please bill the time to my matter. I appreciate the help.

Best,
Desmond Parkwright
